posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Our first sojourn was Ra, F6 Wraith, Santa Guise, Chrono-Ranger and Haka facing off against advanced Ambuscade in Omnitron-IV. It was a surprisingly rough game, and everyone finished with 3 HP or fewer. Amby has some crazy synergy with Omni-IV!
 
Next it was advanced La Capitan in Dok'thorath Capital, versus DW Nightmist, F6 Tempest, F6 Bunker, Legacy and Eternal Haka. Why was Legacy the only non-variant? Only the randomizer knows. I learned that Tempest can actually Sacrifice cards of his that are under La Capitan. He's useful for something after all! I'm never not bringing him against her again! I suspect this revelation completely demoralized her; she only flipped once, and never got any of her really nasty cards out. The heroes kicked her kiester and how. Things ended by bouncing a Rampage off the Elder Amulet.
 
Then I had a friendly multiplayer game with a couple nice d00dz: Wraith, F6 Tempest and Redeemer Fanatic against Voss in Atlantis. Mega-nerd Voss beat up our Tempest, and I learned the dangers of healing too much. Or too little. :( Not even a late-game Wrathful Retribution could turn things around. Dumb ol' Atlantis.
 
Lastly, a fight versus the advanced Ennead, with Legacy, AZ, GI Bunker, Visionary and Santa Guise in the Tomb of Anubis, wow, such thematic, very Egypt! First they destroyed Christmas, then they destroyed the world. But at least fighting the Ennead is always a fun rout, y'know? (Man, between Cold Snap, Demoralization and External Combustion, I was able to do a ton of damage to them before Nuit even fell!)

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Citizen Dawn wanted to make the Tomb of Anubis her base for advanced dealings. Chrono-Ranger, Omnitron-U and the Scholar of the Infinite said, "lol no." Despite an ongoing scarab problem, they were able to stack the deck so Dawn succumbed to the very traps she'd tried to harness for her own twisted ends.
 
Then it was off to Insula Primalis, where Sky-Scraper, Nightmist, GI Bunker and Guise tried to stop advanced Deadline from killing the dinosaurs. It came down to the wire, like, three heroes down but next turn we win, and then Deadline had to go and kill the dinosaurs after all. :| But he was super-sad about it, so I guess it's okay. >:|
 
For a change of pace, I decided to accept the RNG's offer of Argent Adept, Tempest, Santa Guise and EWAZ versus Heroic Infinitor at Rook City, and not play advanced. Azzy and Guise went down in a hail of insanity, and I found out you can't really use Into the Stratosphere against HI, but he might be the one villain where Rook City isn't so bad, and maybe even beneficial. Gotta get those Machinations out, after all! Things ended as they usually do, with Infinitor crazying himself to victory. :D
 
After an aborted attempt at starting a multiplayer game, it was right back to Rook City, where Sky-Scarper, Horus Ra, Grandpa Legacy and Captain Cosmic tried to stop Baron Blade from bombing the crap out of it. Sadly, while Blade learned that destroying a cesspool does not make it any more awful a place to be, the heroes learned that even a sun god's power has its limits. :(
 
Ambuscade at the Enclave is always a nice, easy fight though! Argent Adept, Chrono-Ranger, Omnitron-X and Guise sure seemed to think so!
 
Then came a trip to Megalopolis, so Ra, DW Expatriette and Sky-Scraper could see what was up with that big, advanced Colosseum that had just appeared in the city limits... The answer was pain. Lots and lots of pain. But most of it was thanks to Sky-Scraper's firey clapping. (Thank you, Flesh of the Sun God!)
 
Lastly, Legacy, Bunker, Ra, Argent Adept and Guise versus advanced Akash-Bhuta in the Block. It was a good fight, but in one glorious round of suffering, everything fell apart. Ah well.
 
Total Games: 398

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
A challenge I've wanted to try for a while is beating Heroic Infinitor on his Overcome by Manifestations side, after purposefully 'incapping' him. I took Legacy, Haka, Redeemer Fanatic, the Scholar and TLT along for the ride in Silver Gulch. It took less than two rounds to beat Infinitor down. He was no doubt confused and ultimately justified in his betrayal of the heroes. Then came the hard part. Well, okay, it's not that hard, at least not when you've got Legacy around. Infinitor's healing can be hard to keep up with, but any method of keeping him from dealing damage shuts him down hard. It's especially good if you don't take out any of his Projections on his front side, so he doesn't deal damage when he flips. In the end, Haka finished things off in style, with a hand-dump Haka of Battle for more than twice Inifinitor's remaining HP. (I'm disappointed the game doesn't have a different incap image for him on this side though.)
 
Another thing I needed to do involved facing Citizen Dawn in the Time Cataclysm, with Argent Adept, Guise, Omnitron-X, Dark Visionary and Rook City Wraith for maximum deck-control potential. I got lucky because her first card play was Devastating Aurora, allowing me to Suggest it on top of her deck once I was ready. It took a few rounds, and almost two entire runs through the environment deck, but I was able to learn that, when Fixed Point is in play, Devastating Aurora will destroy it first (being unable to destroy any hero cards), and then take out the rest of the environment cards. Important! Oh yeah, and I guess the heroes beat the villain, too. Guise had a great last round. :V
